title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from the previous page): T^+_{1,1} ≅ SL(2,Z) is the Teichmüller (mapping class) group of type (1,1). Its quotient T'_{1,1} = SL(2,Z)/{±1} contains the level-2 kernel π_{0,3} = Γ(2)/{±1}, which is free on two generators and is the fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. The quotient is S_3 ≅ SL(2,Z/2). The absolute Galois group Γ_Q acts by outer action on the profinite completions. This gives an extension N'_{1,1} ≅ M_{0,3} of Γ_Q by \hat T'_{1,1} ≅ \hat Γ_{0,3}, which is itself an extension of S_3 by \hat π_{0,3}.

On the previous page it was recorded that the outer action of Γ_Q on \hat π_{0,3} is faithful (Belyi) and commutes with the outer action of S_3.

This page reinterprets that commutation:
- It follows from the triviality of the outer action of Γ_Q on S_3 ≅ SL(2,Z/2).
- In the present view, this triviality is a special case of a general fact. The outer action of Γ_Q on the congruence quotient SL(2,Z/n) factors through a faithful action of (Z/n)^*/((Z/n)^*)^2, via the cyclotomic character mod n reduced mod squares.
- Concretely, conjugation by diag(χ(σ),1) is inner modulo SL_2 and scalars exactly when det is a square.
- For n = 2 the group (Z/2)^* is trivial, so the action is trivial. For n ≥ 3 this fails, since φ(n) is even and −1 is not a square at least in the cases relevant here.

So the 'trivial' commutation relation is the first case of subtler 'congruence relations'. Grothendieck proposes to express these directly through the outer action of Γ_Q on \hat π_{0,3}:
- Introduce Π(2m) = ker(\hat π_{0,3} → SL(2,Z/2m)/{±1}). These are open normal subgroups, stable under S_3; they are the principal congruence subgroups Γ(2m) inside Γ(2).
- On the next page he introduces the full congruence map φ_∞ : \hat π_{0,3} → SL(2,\hat Z)', with kernel π(∞) (the congruence kernel) and image the level-2 kernel.
- He states the 'condition des congruences': the Galois (or putative GT-type) outer action preserves the π(2m) and π(∞). On the quotients it is given by the cyclotomic character modulo squares, acting through \hat Z^×/\hat Z^{×2} or (Z/2m)^*/squares.

In modern terms, this is the compatibility of the Galois action on π_1(M_{1,1}) ⊗ \bar Q (or on the Legendre family over P^1 − {0,1,∞}) with the Tate-module representation into GL_2(\hat Z), where det = cyclotomic character. Grothendieck singles it out as a structural constraint on the image of Γ_Q in Out(\hat π_{0,3}).
errors: Minor: 'n ≠ 1,2 i.e. n ≥ 3' is fine. (Z/n)^*/squares is nontrivial for all n ≥ 3 because φ(n) is even, so the claim is correct.
Notation is loose: Sl(2,2m) stands for SL(2,Z/2m), and the prime denotes the quotient by ±1. Nothing wrong mathematically on this page.

ideas.what: Triviality of the Galois outer action on S_3 = SL(2,Z/2) explained as the n=2 case of an action through the cyclotomic character mod n modulo squares on SL(2,Z/n)
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the outer Galois representation on π_1(M_{1,1}) with the adelic Tate-module representation (det = cyclotomic character)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Deligne–Rapoport, Shimura); in the anabelian setting Ihara, Nakamura, Matsumoto
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse explicitly as far as I know; related themes in La Longue Marche (unpublished)

ideas.what: Congruence kernels Π(2m), π(∞) ⊂ \hat π_{0,3} as S_3-stable characteristic-like subgroups, and a 'congruence condition' on outer actions of Γ_Q (or GT-type groups) on \hat π_{0,3}
ideas.modern_name: Congruence subgroup kernel of \hat F_2 = \hat Γ(2) → SL_2(\hat Z); GT action and congruence quotients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara / Nakamura / Lochak–Schneps-type work on GT and the modular group; unsure about a specific congruence statement for GT

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes making explicit the 'congruence condition' as a constraint on outer actions on \hat π_{0,3}: preservation of all congruence kernels π(2m), with the induced action given by the cyclotomic character mod squares. This could serve as a defining condition for a GT-like group. Whether \hat{GT} automatically satisfies it is a natural question; it is only partially addressed in the literature as far as I know.
missed.quote: relations congruentielles nettement plus subtiles. On peut essayer de les exprimer directement en termes de l'opération ext. de Γ_Q sur \hat Π_{0,3}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This bears on the relation between \hat{GT} and Γ_Q, and on the congruence-subgroup / modular aspects of GT (e.g. GT actions on profinite SL_2(Z) and on modular curves). For Γ_Q the statement is classical, so the novelty is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: For Γ_Q the content is the classical compatibility of the outer action on π_1 of the modular / Legendre tower with the cyclotomic determinant on SL_2(\hat Z). The framing as 'congruence conditions' generalizing the S_3 triviality is a nice heuristic. It is not a new result, though possibly an under-explored constraint for GT-type groups.
transcription_corrections: The group acting is written like Γ_Q / Π_Q. Given the previous page it is most likely Γ_Q (absolute Galois group of Q).
'(Z/2Z)^*_{/2}' means (Z/2Z)^*/((Z/2Z)^*)^2, i.e. units modulo squares. Likewise '(Z/nZ)^*_2'.
'en autres termes triviale' is likely 'en outre triviale' or 'en apparence triviale'; uncertain.
The struck word before 'directement' is 'façon'; 'plus' is struck at the line end.
